change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Fail-fast on multiple crypto providers removed; equal-order providers are now picked silently
findings.body: Before this change, more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw `IllegalStateException`. Now the providers are sorted by `order()` and the first one wins. The default, elytron and fips1402 providers all return 200 (`DefaultCryptoProvider.java:84`, `WildFlyElytronProvider.java:77`, `FIPS1402Provider.java:115`). If two of them are on the classpath, the winner depends on `ServiceLoader` iteration order, which follows classpath order and is stable in the sort. A FIPS deployment that also has the default provider on the classpath could then silently run non-FIPS crypto. The only trace is a `debug` log. The misconfiguration error is the only safeguard that was removed, and only the intended authz-client case (100 vs 200) needs the new behaviour. Suggested fix: throw the previous error when the top two providers have the same `order()`. At minimum, log the ignored providers at WARN.

findings.title: New abstract `order()` breaks every external CryptoProvider implementation
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI interface in `common`. Adding an abstract `int order()` stops any out-of-tree implementation from compiling. A custom provider that was already compiled will fail with `AbstractMethodError` inside the sort in `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`. A `default int order() { return 200; }` (or similar) would keep source and binary compatibility and still allow the authz-client provider to override it.

findings.title: Dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build two `ASN1Encoder` instances and discard them. The result is rebuilt on lines 117-121. Remove them.

findings.title: Malformed DER yields unchecked exceptions instead of IOException
findings.body: `readInteger` on `02 80` gets length -1 from `readLength` (indefinite form), and `read(-1)` throws `NegativeArraySizeException`. A zero-length INTEGER makes `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throw `NumberFormatException`. `readNext` also mishandles a nested indefinite length (`length += reset()` with length -1). The `ECDSACryptoProvider` contract and the callers declare `IOException`, and the current callers happen to catch `Exception`. The only caller today feeds this decoder trusted JDK-produced DER, so impact is low. Reject negative lengths in `readLength` and `readInteger`, and reject empty integers, so the decoder fails with `IOException`. Also, `readTagNumber` masks the class and constructed bits, so a primitive tag 0x10 passes as a SEQUENCE. Compare the full tag byte.

findings.title: Test uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks self round-trip
findings.body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` gives a 256-bit curve key. For ES384 and ES512 the signature is therefore r and s of at most 32 bytes padded into 48- and 66-byte halves. The real P-384 and P-521 value sizes are never exercised. The key and signature are random, so the cases that matter (high-bit r or s, short r or s that needs padding or a stripped leading zero) are hit only by chance and the test can pass or fail from run to run. The assertion compares the provider's output with its own re-encoding. It never checks that the re-encoded DER verifies with `Signature.verify`, and it never compares against the BC implementation. Suggested: generate a key per curve (`secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`), verify the re-encoded DER with `Signature.verify`, and add fixed vectors with short and high-bit r and s. `hamcrest` is added to the pom (`authz/client/pom.xml:67-71`) but is not used by the test.

findings.title: First-wins CryptoIntegration.init in a library entry point
findings.body: `CryptoIntegration.init` does nothing once a provider has been set, and it uses the classloader passed by the first caller. If an application calls `AuthzClient.create` before the intended full provider is initialised (for example, crypto jars loaded by a different classloader than the authz-client jar), only the 100-order provider sees `AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()`. It is then latched for the whole JVM, and every unsupported operation (`getCertificateUtils`, `getSignature`, ...) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Is this ordering scenario considered, and is it documented?

contracts.equivalent_path: Server: KeycloakApplication calls CryptoIntegration.init(KeycloakApplication.class.getClassLoader()); CLI: Globals.java:44 calls CryptoIntegration.init(cl). All other create() overloads delegate to create(Configuration).
contracts.before_after: Before: authz-client never initialised CryptoIntegration, so any core code calling CryptoIntegration.getProvider() threw IllegalStateException. After: init loads providers via ServiceLoader; with only the authz-client jar, AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) is chosen. When a real provider (order 200) is also present, it wins. The init is skipped if a provider is already set.
contracts.visible_effect: ECDSA (ES256/384/512) signature conversion in core works inside the authz client. Other provider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException. BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER becomes the name of the JDK provider behind the default KeyStore type.
contracts.failure_mode: If no provider is found, init throws IllegalStateException from create(). With two providers of equal order, an arbitrary one is silently chosen (see finding on CryptoIntegration). A provider latched earlier by another caller is never replaced.

contracts.action: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider: new hand-written ASN.1 DER encoder/decoder for ECDSA signatures
contracts.equivalent_path: BCECDSACryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER / asn1derToConcatenatedRS in crypto/default, which use BouncyCastle ASN1 classes.
contracts.before_after: The new concatenatedRSToASN1DER has the same structure as the BC version: pad to len+1, build BigIntegers, DER sequence. asn1derToConcatenatedRS parses with the custom decoder and pads or truncates like X9IntegerConverter. Length handling of the input signature is equivalent: a shorter input throws an unchecked exception and extra trailing bytes are ignored, as in the BC version.
contracts.visible_effect: ES* JWS sign and verify in the client yields the same bytes as the server's default provider for valid input.
contracts.failure_mode: The verifier contexts catch Exception and wrap it in VerificationException, so malformed input fails visibly. The decoder can throw non-IOException runtime exceptions for malformed DER (see finding).

summary: The PR adds a lightweight CryptoProvider to the authz client, with a custom ASN.1 ECDSA converter. It also adds `order()` to the SPI and replaces the multiple-provider error in `CryptoIntegration` with priority-based selection. The ECDSA conversion matches the BC implementation's behaviour for valid input. Main concerns: equal-order providers (default, elytron and fips all return 200) are now chosen silently, and the abstract `order()` breaks external provider implementations. Smaller points: dead code in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, unchecked exceptions from the decoder on malformed DER, and a weak test that uses a P-256 key for every ES algorithm and only checks a self round-trip.
